https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/n.text: Ukraine launches one of its largest attacks, killing at least six in Russia By PA News Agency Share 0 Comments 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Ukraine has launched hundreds of drones across Russia, killing at least six people in one of Kyiv’s largest aerial attacks of the war. Russia’s Ministry of Defence said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight. About 600 were detected heading toward the Russian capital, Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, with a third destroyed over the Moscow region. An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone hit a private home in the Moscow region, local governor Andrey Vorobyov said. Firefighters try to put out a fire at a book market in Kyiv (Dan Bashakov/AP) He also confirmed that a Ukrainian attack had sparked a blaze at a warehouse belonging to Russian retail giant Wildberries. Images shared by Russian media outlets from the town of Podolsk showed columns of black smoke rising from the site. Another drone attack targeted three towns in Russia’s south-western Rostov region, killing five people, local governor Yury Slyusar said. The attack, with more than 150 drones, damaged several homes and a railway station and sparked a forest fire. Ukraine has stepped up its attacks on Russia this year, with long-range missiles and swarms of drones increasingly targeting military industries and energy facilities. A bookseller reacts after a Russian missile attack in Kyiv (Francisco Seco/AP) It has also increasingly targeted giant Wildberries depots, burning billions of pounds of merchandise and bringing the war home to the Russian public more than four years into Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. A Russian missile attack on Ukraine’s Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media on Sunday. He also said that one person had been killed in the city of Sumy. Another Russian attack on Kyiv sparked fires throughout the Ukrainian capital and injured six people. “Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure,” Mr Zelensky said. “Since this morning, air raid alerts have continued in many regions – the Russians launched another wave of drones.” The aftermath of the strike in Kyiv (Francisco Seco/AP) Russia’s Ministry of Defence said on Sunday that it had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih and several military-industrial sites in Kyiv, including a manufacturing facility for Ukraine’s Flamingo missiles. The domestically produced missiles are increasingly key to Ukraine’s long-range attacks on Russia, with Mr Zelensky announcing on Saturday that Kyiv had used the weapons to attack a rocket research and production centre in Samara, about 560 miles from the Ukrainian border. Romania’s Ministry of National Defence said on Sunday that a Spanish Air and Space Force F-18 fighter jet shot down a drone that had entered Romanian air space. The drone’s entry into the Nato member’s air space was detected by surveillance systems, the ministry said, about 15 miles north of the eastern city of Galati, near the border with Moldova. Photograph: Oliver Furrer/Getty Images/Image Source Milwaukee Team of skydivers drop in to help survivors of a plane crash in Wisconsin Recreational jumpers used their training as paramedics to treat crash victims before ground crews arrived Richard Luscombe Tue 29 Sep 2026 12.47 EDT Last modified on Tue 29 Sep 2026 12.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A team of experienced skydivers recently dropped in to help at a plane crash they happened to witness in Wisconsin – and used their training as paramedics to treat a seriously injured victim before ground-based rescue crews arrived. The single-engine plane carrying four people crashed in a cornfield near East Troy on Sunday, watched by the occupants of a Skydive Milwaukee aircraft who were preparing for an afternoon of recreational jumping. “He kind of banked up and then he disappeared behind the trees, and we were all waiting for him to show back up,” John Bechtel, one of several veteran skydivers on board, told Wisconsin ABC News affiliate WISN . “We all looked at each other and said, ‘Did we just see a plane crash?’” Wisconsin police investigating fraternity for hazing after men found in basement Read more Bechtel, who has more than 30 years of skydiving experience, said he and two colleagues decided to jump straight to the site of the crash after calling in what they saw to authorities on the ground. One of the jumpers, who like Bechtel is also a former paramedic, helped a woman with a serious head injury until an EMT crew arrived by ambulance. “The timing couldn’t have been any better. Had we left five minutes earlier, we wouldn’t have seen it. If we left 15 minutes later, we wouldn’t have been able to get there to assist,” Bechtel said. “I’m just glad that we were able to do what we could and get in and help.” Officials in Walworth county said three passengers in the crashed plane were taken to hospital and the fourth was treated at the scene. All are expected to survive. Aerial footage on the WISN website showed the aircraft, a Beechcraft 35-A33 Debonair manufactured in 1961, upright on the ground with one of its wings detached. Jonah Johnston, the pilot of the jump plane, told air traffic controllers in an emergency call: “I have a plane crash, just south of East Troy. He’s in a field. I can drop a load of skydivers right over them to potentially help aid.” Kevin Flynn, another of the skydivers, told Milwaukee news outlet WDJT that he and Bechtel started calling out as soon as they hit the ground because they couldn’t see the plane through the tall corn. “I got in there and started doing the Marco Polo game to get a response,” he said. “People started yelling at me so I could dial in where I was going. “It could’ve been a lot worse for those poor people in that crash, no fatalities. I know it’s a terrible thing to happen, but I think it’s a wonderful outcome.” In a statement, Skydive Milwaukee said: “A few members of our skydiving community who are trained [emergency medical technicians] were already airborne in our jump plane and jumped out to assist at the scene, which was difficult to access from the road. “We’re grateful they were able to help when they were needed.” The identities of the victims have not been released. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) opened an inquiry into the cause of the crash and an investigator arrived at the site on Sunday afternoon.
